newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close higher, index led by KEPCO rise.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close higher, index led by KEPCO rise.

text.p: Stocks closed higher on Tuesday in a technical rebound following six consecutive days of declines, brokers said.
They said the trading sentiment was also helped by news that the ruling party and an investment companies' association asked for government steps to boost the stock market.
The composite index ended 10.66 points, or 1.54 percent, higher at a provisional 702.83.
"The rebound was basically technical, although the news of requests for boosting measures helped buoy the mood," said Koh Soon-shik of LG Securities.
Brokers said the index rise was so large because Korea Electric Power Corp, the heaviest-weighted stock on the composite index, gained 6.25 percent or 1,500 won to 25,500.
"About six points of rise in today's composite index came from KEPCO," said Yoo Nam-gil of Hyundai Securities. "Foreign buying and local institutional buying together pushed up the KEPCO shares."

The ruling New Korea Party and the Korea Investment Trust Companies' Association separately urged the government to take steps to boost the ailing stock market. The Finance Ministry did not immediately respond to the requests.
"The news had only limited impact on the market today because investors were unsure about whether and how the government would accept the requests," said Yoo of Hyundai.
They called for a delay in the government's planned sale of stakes in Korea Telecom and other state-run companies to ease fears about a share oversupply.

Hwan Yung Steel fell 490 won to its daily limit of 5,710 in the morning session shortly before the exchange suspended trading of Hwan Yung shares due to rumours that the company faced a final deadline to pay back debt by the end of the day.
